subject: Getting reasonable axis breaks with scale_x_log10 and very small x values

messages.author: 6a95d2ee62a86e9f
messages.subject: Getting reasonable axis breaks with scale_x_log10 and very small x values
parts:
I have a variable plotting on the x-axis whose values range from
~1e-18 to ~ 1e-13. I use scale_x_log10(), but only get a single
break, at the minimum value in the data. I tried adding
breaks=c(1e-18, 1e-16, 1e-14), but that also gives a single break, now
at 1e-18. I can change x units from moles to pico-moles, and that
gives reasonable axis breaks, but I'm curious why I cannot do this
with the original units.

Woody Setzer

messages.author: 6a95d2ee62a86e9f
messages.subject: Re: Getting reasonable axis breaks with scale_x_log10 and very small x values
parts:
Sure:

library(ggplot2)

df <- data.frame(x = 10^runif(80, -19,-13), y=rnorm(80))

p <- ggplot(df, aes(x,y)) + geom_point() + scale_x_log10()
print(p)

On my setup (R version 2.15.0 Patched (2012-04030 r59275) and ggplot2 version 0.9.0,
this gives a scatter plot with a single x break, at 2.259244e-19, which is min(df$x).

Woody

messages.author: e4aec126ff1dca22
messages.subject: Re: Getting reasonable axis breaks with scale_x_log10 and very small x values
parts:
This may help as well (looks numerical) -

n <- 10

# original demonstration of problem
df <- data.frame(x = 10^runif(n, -19, -13), y = rnorm(n))
qplot(x, y, data = df) + scale_x_log10()

# happens on normal scale, too
qplot(x, y, data = df)

# this helps to see where it happens
u <- runif(n); y <- rnorm(n)
df <- NULL
for(k in 1:18){
  df <- rbind(df, data.frame(x = 10^(-k-u), y = y, g = k))
}

qplot(x, y, data = df) # ok
qplot(x, y, data = df) + scale_x_log10() # ok
qplot(x, y, data = df) + facet_wrap(~ g, scales = 'free_x')
qplot(x, y, data = df) + facet_wrap(~ g, scales = 'free_x') + scale_x_log10()

david.
